final.title: Measuring late payment terms without guessing
final.body:
If you want to measure late payment terms, keep the decision narrow: are you still tracking due dates, actual payment dates, and follow-up status by memory or spreadsheet, or do you have a repeatable check that flags overdue invoices before they turn into a cash-flow surprise?

The useful question is not whether to redesign finance. It is whether one recurring task can be made more reliable: compare the invoice date, agreed terms, and payment date; flag anything past due; and keep a simple log of what was late. Any collection action stays with a human. Money movement stays human too. The build stays technical; the decision stays human.

For a small business, that is usually enough to test the workflow without pretending it is bigger than it is. If you are unsure whether the work is frequent enough, ask: how many invoices do you issue each month, and how do you currently know which ones are late?

A practical next step is to audit one week of invoices. Note which were paid on time, which were late, and how long manual review took. Treat that as a self-check on the process, not a claim about results. If the pattern is consistent, you have a bounded workflow worth looking at; if not, you have answered the question without building anything at all.
